questions.q: Why does this lesson say a System Architect must widen the security lens beyond what an Application Architect typically worries about?
options: Because profiles, permission sets, and field-level security no longer matter at the enterprise level
Because every integration boundary is a potential path for data to leave Salesforce's security model or for a threat to enter through a trusted connection
Because Application Architects are not permitted to discuss security at all
Because Salesforce Shield makes all other security considerations unnecessary
questions.explain: The lesson explains that every integration (batch sync, Remote Call-In, data virtualization feed) is a potential path for data or threats to cross between security models, which is why a System Architect's security scope has to extend beyond the org's own boundary.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four commonly-cited Salesforce Shield components described in this lesson?
options: Platform Encryption
Salesforce Connect
Change Data Capture
Developer Pro Sandbox
questions.explain: The lesson describes Salesforce Shield as commonly covering Platform Encryption, Field Audit Trail, Event Monitoring, and Data Detect -- Platform Encryption specifically protects sensitive data at rest at the field, file, and attachment level.

questions.q: What does this lesson say Salesforce Shield does and does not cover?
options: Shield secures Salesforce's own data and activity, but says nothing about the security of the ERP, middleware, or data warehouse the data also touches elsewhere in the enterprise
Shield automatically extends its protections to every external system Salesforce integrates with
Shield replaces the need for any identity and access management strategy across the enterprise
Shield covers network security for every system in the company, not just Salesforce
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that Shield only protects what happens inside Salesforce -- a System Architect still has to account for the security posture of every other system the data touches as it moves through the enterprise.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what question should a System Architect ask whenever designing an integration boundary, regarding security?
options: Whether the integration can be built using the newest available Salesforce API, regardless of security implications
What security travels with the boundary -- such as whether data needs encryption in transit and whether the external system's access controls match the data's sensitivity
Whether the integration boundary needs a screenshot for documentation purposes
Whether the business has approved the integration's budget
questions.explain: The lesson's practical takeaway is to ask explicitly what security travels with every integration boundary -- encryption in transit, credential exposure, and whether the receiving system's access controls match the data's sensitivity.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does Field Audit Trail do that goes beyond standard Salesforce field history tracking?
options: It blocks all edits to any audited field
It extends field-level change history tracking and retention well beyond what standard field history tracking provides
It encrypts field values so they can never be read by any user
It automatically deletes field history after 24 hours
questions.explain: The lesson describes Field Audit Trail as extending field-level change history tracking and retention well beyond Salesforce's standard field history tracking feature.
